title: Camera
summary: A camera in front of the table, above it, looking down at the plate; the scene scaled to real-world size (the plate 30 cm) so the lights and depth of field behave; lights lowered to match; depth of field focused on the donut at f/1; a square 1080x1080 frame with a touch more zoom.

objects.name: Camera
objects.description: the shot: front, above, looking down at the donuts

expected_result: A square shot from the front and above: the plate with the two donuts in the middle, the croissant back left and the mug back right, the donut sharp and the back softly blurred, lit by the spot.

steps.note: Shift+A > Camera, then View > Lock camera to view and frame it: in front of the table and above, looking down at the plate, the croissant and mug at the back
the scene was built far too big (plate 6-7 m): A then S to shrink everything so the plate is ~30 cm; lights and depth of field depend on real scale
at the new scale the lights are 20x closer, so the same look needs ~1/400 of the power (the tutor: 5000 -> 10); radius scaled too
the spot the same way (the tutor: 7000 -> 100)
Depth of Field on, Focus Object = the donut, F-stop 1: what is not at the donut's distance goes soft
Output properties: a square 1080 x 1080 frame (the tutor still uses Eevee here; headless renders with Cycles)
the square frame changed the framing, so a bit more zoom (focal length)
